faq.subtitle: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
faq.q1: How does the work process work?
faq.a1: We start with an introductory call to understand your project, your goals and the context. Then I prepare a detailed proposal with times, costs and phases. I work iteratively, with regular checkpoints to keep you updated.
faq.q2: How long does it take to build a website?
faq.a2: It depends on the complexity. A corporate website takes 3-6 weeks, an e-commerce 6-10 weeks, a custom web app 2-4 months. I will always give you an accurate estimate after understanding the requirements of your project.
faq.q3: Do you work remotely or only in Sicily?
faq.a3: I work mainly remotely and collaborate with clients all over Italy and abroad. Communication takes place via email, video call and shared project management tools.
faq.a4: Yes. Each project includes a post-launch support period. We can then define a continuous maintenance plan based on your needs.
faq.q5: Can I manage the site autonomously after delivery?
faq.a5: Absolutely. For WordPress and CMS projects I always provide a training session. For React web apps I provide you with documentation and full access to the code.

chario.meta_desc: Digital high fidelity. Premium website created with my proprietary Sophia theme for an uncompromising acoustic and visual experience.
chario.hero_desc: Translating 50 years of craftsmanship excellence into an uncompromising web experience. Minimalist UI/UX design and full-stack development of a custom architecture for an elegant and ultra-performant digital ecosystem.
chario.ch1_title1: When the product is analog, but
chario.ch1_p1: Chario Hifi is a historic Italian brand producing audio speakers since 1975, famous worldwide for its hand-carved solid wood cabinets. Yet, despite the absolute prestige of the physical products, their online presence no longer reflected the prestige and high-end nature of their products.
chario.ch1_p2: The previous site was slow, fragmented and — paradoxically for a Made in Italy excellence — available exclusively in English. A radical repositioning was needed: a visual redesign to enhance the material details of the speakers and a new multilingual architecture, finally starting from Italian, to give the company back its true voice.
chario.ch3_p1: For the user interface, the fundamental rule was "subtract". I adopted an essential but profoundly editorial approach: the use of extremely thin serif fonts for the titles, paired with a solid grotesque to ensure maximum readability in the descriptive paragraphs.
chario.ch3_p2: The dominant colors faithfully reflect the natural palette of the speakers: deep burgundy, dark wood shades and a dusty cream for the background. No rounded buttons, no superfluous shadows. The white (or negative) space has been strategically maximized to give every single photograph the breathing room it deserves, allowing the user to get lost in the product details without any visual distraction.
chario.ch4_p1: From a technical point of view, the project is based on a completely custom WordPress architecture. I abandoned classic (and heavy) visual builders to develop Sophia, a modular PHP parent theme, coupled with a specific child theme for Chario. All style logic, fluid animations (managed via GSAP and ScrollTrigger) and interactions have been encapsulated and isolated. The result is instant front-end rendering and pure code, capable of supporting the 3D renders and high-resolution photographs necessary for the luxury market without hesitation (jank).
chario.ch4_p2: The real jewel in the crown is the Chario HiFi Builder: a proprietary manifest-driven page builder. Through a real-time JavaScript connection (PostMessage API), the client can edit content and see the results instantly in the preview iframe, keeping the layout locked. Finally, to ensure global robustness, I engineered the Zenith Recovery Engine: a proprietary fallback system that maps translations and URL paths directly at the code level, ensuring the site never "breaks" during language switching.
chario.ch5_p1: The result is a web ecosystem that converts not through aggressive Call to Actions, but through true aesthetic infatuation. From the homepage to the complexity of the multilingual backend, every single component has been engineered and designed with a single purpose: to serve the sound and pay homage to the brand's excellence.

sophia.meta_desc: The invisible engine of luxury editorial projects. Sophia Theme redefines code speed and cleanliness standards, taking performance to the next level.
sophia.hero_desc: A proprietary, modular, and performance-oriented WordPress framework. Developed to replace heavy traditional page builders and give web projects pure, instant, and totally scalable code.
sophia.ch1_p1: Most premium themes on the market carry an enormous technical debt, sacrificing performance (Core Web Vitals) in the name of fake versatility. The result is slow websites, overloaded with unused scripts and impossible to scale. Sophia was born to solve this equation: to provide robust technical foundations that allow the development of luxury interfaces without any compromise on loading performance.
sophia.ch2_title3: to unleash the power of excellent design."
sophia.ch3_p1: Sophia doesn't just use the classic monolithic functions.php file. Its code is organized into isolated logics: from theme setup to extension management. This modular architecture leverages a Design System based on global CSS variables, making the aesthetic aspect infinitely scalable. In addition, I have natively integrated premium motion libraries like GSAP and ScrollTrigger, allowing cinematic scrolling and complex animations to be managed without affecting performance.
sophia.ch4_p1: The true heart of the system is the Sophia Builder: a proprietary manifest-driven visual page builder. Instead of saving complex layouts in the database, it decodes JSON files to instantly generate the administrative interface. Thanks to the PostMessage API, modifications synchronize in real time within the preview iframe. To ensure maximum multilingual stability, Sophia is also equipped with the Zenith Recovery Engine, a proprietary fallback system that maps and translates strings at the code level.
sophia.ch5_p1: Sophia is not just a theme; it's a highly customized and meticulous framework. It guarantees total editorial control over content with lightning-fast frontend performance, as the final output always remains pure PHP and HTML5 code with asynchronous loading. An ecosystem designed to last and scale.

storagehub.meta_desc: Intelligent inventory and warehouse management system built as a team project within AWS re/Start Academy 2025/2026. Decoupled full-stack architecture — Django 4, React 18, PostgreSQL — with multi-provider AI (OpenAI GPT-4 + Google Gemini) and production-grade AWS cloud infrastructure.
storagehub.hero_desc: Built within the AWS re/Start Dev, Cloud & Product Academy 2025/2026, StorageHub is a complete inventory and warehouse management system that transforms the chaos of spreadsheets into a single source of truth, assisted by artificial intelligence. AWS cloud architecture with ECS Fargate, Multi-AZ RDS and WAF — engineered for enterprise scale from the very first line of code.
storagehub.ch1_title1: When spreadsheets cost more than they seem.
storagehub.ch1_p1: Traditional inventory management is one of the most silent sources of loss in companies: spreadsheets misaligned across departments, sudden stockouts that halt sales, and zero real-time communication between decision-makers and warehouse staff. The cost is not only financial — it is cognitive. Every 'where are the stock levels for that product?' is an interruption, an email, a wait. StorageHub was born from a precise question: what if the warehouse could speak directly to management, in real time, without intermediaries?
storagehub.ch2_title1: "When managing my company's logistics, I want
storagehub.ch2_title3: of stock levels — to make fast decisions and ensure products are always available for sale."
storagehub.ch3_p1: The project was developed within a five-person team at AWS re/Start Academy, with the role of Full-Stack Lead Developer. The starting point was not technology but real workflow analysis: who the users are, what they do, where they lose time. Two radically different profiles emerged — the Admin (strategic view: finances, suppliers, AI reports, threshold configuration) and the Warehouse Operator (focused operations: IN/OUT movements, immediate alerts, zero distractions) — which drove every architecture and interface decision.
storagehub.ch4_p1: The architecture is intentionally decoupled: Django 4 backend with Django REST Framework on PostgreSQL, React 18 frontend with REST-only communication. Every movement recorded in the warehouse instantly updates the management dashboard and recalculates total inventory value. The database maintains an immutable log of every operation — no silent edits, everything tracked, everything reversible. Full audit trail: who did what, when, with which quantity.
storagehub.ch5_p1: The result is a management system that does not merely record data, but actively participates in business decisions. By replacing misaligned spreadsheets with a secure, fast, AI-assisted infrastructure, StorageHub transforms the warehouse from a cost centre into an efficiency engine. The project proved something that wasn't obvious: technical complexity — full CRUD, multi-role management, integrated AI, immutable logs, production-grade AWS infrastructure — and ease of use are not opposites. They can and must coexist, if design decisions come before technology decisions.
storagehub.ch3_p2: I designed two separate dashboards sharing the same PostgreSQL backend but displaying radically different information. The choice to implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with JWT tokens was not merely technical — it was above all a design decision. A warehouse operator should not see financial margins: it distracts and creates anxiety. A manager should not wade through operational movements: it overloads and slows decisions. The simplicity of each interface is the direct result of that separation. Every field, every button, every notification is there because it serves that specific person — and nothing else.
storagehub.ch4_p2: The innovative core is the multi-provider AI system: parallel integration of OpenAI GPT-4 and Google Gemini with contextual prompts that analyse stock in real time and suggest reorders in natural language. Supporting two providers instead of one was deliberate: it reduces dependency on a single service, allows recommendations to be compared, and guarantees operational continuity if one provider experiences downtime. The cloud infrastructure runs on AWS with WAF + CloudFront for global distribution, ALB + ECS Fargate for the containerised backend, Multi-AZ RDS PostgreSQL for high availability, ElastiCache Redis for sessions and cache — with an estimated operational cost of approximately €400/month.

freelens.meta_desc: SaaS project management platform designed specifically for freelancers and independent professionals. React 18, TypeScript, Supabase with RLS, serverless Edge Functions and Stripe integration. Real-time financial dashboard with contextual AI assistant.
freelens.hero_desc: A SaaS management platform built for independent professionals who want to stop working at a loss without knowing it. A complete ecosystem for financial tracking, real margin control, and business optimisation — with an AI assistant that reads your context and suggests the right moves.
freelens.ch1_title1: The antidote to technical bankruptcy.
freelens.ch1_p1: Working hard doesn't always mean working profitably. The endemic problem among freelancers isn't a lack of work — it's a lack of visibility: unbilled hours, poorly estimated projects, sliding deadlines, and margins that evaporate quietly. Freelens was built to solve exactly this: give independent professionals the same financial clarity that a good CFO would bring to a structured company. Not another task manager. A financial partner that actually understands how independent work functions.
freelens.ch2_title1: "Regain control of your time. An ecosystem where financial health finally becomes clear, measurable, and assisted by AI."
freelens.ch3_p1: The interface is designed as a fluid Single Page Application with React 18 and TypeScript. I chose a premium aesthetic — glassmorphism, dynamic gradients, calibrated micro-interactions — for a precise reason: administration is an activity people delay because they perceive it as tedious and anxiety-inducing. If the interface is beautiful and pleasant to use, the psychological barrier drops. TanStack Query handles caching to eliminate perceived loading times; Recharts makes every financial KPI readable at a glance without opening a spreadsheet.
freelens.ch4_p1: The backend relies on PostgreSQL with strict RLS (Row Level Security) policies enforced at database level — not just application level. Every user has exclusive access to their own data, with isolation guaranteed at infrastructure level. The primary added value lies in the serverless Edge Functions: a microservice that powers the AI assistant by reading the professional's real financial context — overdue payments, loss-making projects, upcoming deadlines — and returning strategic suggestions in natural language. Stripe manages premium subscriptions with webhooks for payment state synchronisation.
freelens.ch5_p1: The result is a complete and scalable end-to-end SaaS product combining an impactful interface with a complex data architecture. The hardest challenge wasn't technical — it was positioning: building something freelancers would actually want to use every day, not only when already in crisis. The answer was an interface that makes you feel in control, not under pressure. That shows numbers clearly, not alarmingly. That suggests, not judges.

portfolio.meta_desc: A dual-identity digital system, built to prove that a portfolio can itself be the most complex project in the portfolio.
portfolio.hero_desc: A portfolio that changes its skin depending on who's looking. A dual-identity digital system, built to prove that a portfolio can itself be the most complex project in the portfolio.
portfolio.ch1_title1: Not a portfolio. A system.
portfolio.ch1_p1: The brief was personal: build something that didn't just showcase the work, but embodied the method. A portfolio that was already an answer to the question "how do you think about design?". The solution was a live-switchable dual design system — Editorial and Nebula — two coherent and distinct visual identities the user can alternate in real time, without reloading the page.
portfolio.ch2_title1: "Challenge yourself technically, without losing warmth. The goal wasn't to impress with effects — it was to demonstrate control."
portfolio.ch3_title: The real problem was the CSS, not the design.
portfolio.ch3_p1: Building a design system that switches in real time requires every visual value — colors, typography, spacing, shadows — to be abstracted into CSS variables swapped at the root level. No component can contain hardcoded values. After the first iterations it became clear that the biggest challenge wasn't aesthetics, but systemic consistency: every new component added had to work in both themes without exceptions. The system took approximately 1-2 months to build, most of it spent testing edge cases — hover states, animations, transitions — across both themes simultaneously.
portfolio.ch4_title: Web Audio, Three.js and a favicon that changes with the theme.
portfolio.ch4_p1: The technical stack was chosen to maximise expressiveness without compromising performance: React + Vite for the architecture, Framer Motion for page transitions, Three.js for the 3D canvas in the Nebula theme, Web Audio API for audio response reactive to the active theme, Lenis for smooth scroll, full IT/EN i18n. One detail that sums up the approach: the favicon changes dynamically on theme toggle — a minimal gesture that proves the system is truly end-to-end. Bundle splitting is configured to guarantee LCP under 2.5 seconds even on average connections.
portfolio.ch5_p1: The result is a system where every component — from typography to favicon, from audio to 3D canvas — is engineered around a single idea: that a designer's identity is not monolithic. The portfolio was submitted to Awwwards as a demonstration of a design method, not just an aesthetic outcome. The most honest metric: every person who opens it chooses the theme that reflects them most. That was the objective.

villamasami.meta_desc: The first digital presence for Villa Masami, a B&B in the Agrigento countryside. Brand identity built from scratch — logo, tone of voice, UI — and a bilingual IT/EN WordPress site developed for Carnova.
villamasami.hero_desc: A complete digital debut for a Sicilian B&B near the Valley of the Temples. Full creative freedom: from the MV monogram logo to the bilingual WordPress architecture, everything designed to turn an invisible property into a recognisable destination.
villamasami.ch1_p1: Villa Masami is a B&B in Favara, Agrigento province, a few kilometres from the Valley of the Temples. Rooms with independent keypad access, well-kept outdoor spaces, warm family hospitality. Yet before this project, it had no online presence whatsoever — no website, no visual identity, nothing. The property collected bookings through major platforms but had no voice of its own.
villamasami.ch1_p2: Carnova's brief was clear: build everything from zero, with full creative freedom. The goal was not merely to create a website, but to give the property a coherent, recognisable identity that could live online and offline, in Italian and English, and convert visitors into guests.
villamasami.ch2_title1: "More comfort, less friction: translate the warmth of real hospitality into a seamless digital experience that converts the visitor into a guest from the very first click."
villamasami.ch3_p1: The project started with identity — where every brief should begin. Working with full creative freedom, the starting intuition was to merge the M and V of Villa Masami into a single geometric pictogram, reusable as icon, favicon, and decorative element. The logo — approved on the second of two proposals — captures the property's minimalist elegance without resorting to Sicilian clichés. Clean, scalable, instantly recognisable at any size, from business card to signage.
villamasami.ch3_p2: From there, I built the entire visual system: a warm palette inspired by the stones and light of the Agrigento countryside, typography balancing warmth and clarity, a reassuring and direct tone of voice. With more graphic freedom than any previous project, I was able to make compositional choices I would previously have tempered. The result is an identity that feels Sicilian without being folkloristic — elegant without being cold.
villamasami.ch4_p1: The site is built on WordPress with a visual builder, chosen to allow the client to manage content independently over time. I designed every single view — from homepage to room details — ensuring perfect mobile responsiveness and a bilingual IT/EN architecture that immediately positioned the property in the international tourism market.
villamasami.ch4_p2: Technical completion took around two weeks. Launch timing extended due to client-side factors — typical with family-run hospitality properties where operational priorities take over. But this allowed refinement of details and delivery of a more polished product. Since the site went live, Villa Masami has seen measurable growth in social media presence and an increase in direct booking enquiries — no longer relying exclusively on the major booking platforms.
villamasami.ch5_p1: The result is a digital presence that reflects the soul of the villa: warm, ordered, accessible. A project demonstrating how creative freedom — when guided by a precise brief and careful contextual analysis — produces authentic identities rather than generic solutions. Villa Masami went from digital invisibility to a destination with a face, a voice, and a website that actively works for it. For me, it was also a turning point: the first project where I had enough trust — from the client and from myself — to make bold graphic choices rather than safe ones.

pattiforniture.meta_desc: Digital restyling of Patti Forniture, a historic leading company in Southern Italy for industrial supplies, thermo-hydraulics, and building materials. Built with WordPress.
pattiforniture.hero_desc: The first website for F.lli Patti: not a restyling, but the first ever digital presence for a company with thirty years of history in industrial supplies, thermo-hydraulics, and construction in Southern Italy. Built with Carnova, covering information architecture, user interface, strategic copywriting, and complete WordPress development.
pattiforniture.ch1_p1: For over three decades, F.lli Patti has been a reference point for retailers, installers, and private clients across Southern Italy — thermo-hydraulics, construction, hardware, air conditioning. Thirty years of reputation built on direct relationships, warehouse availability, and sector expertise. Yet in 2026, this solid reality had no online presence whatsoever. No website, no digital showcase. The challenge wasn't to 'refresh' something — it was to build a credible digital presence from scratch for a company that already had immense credibility, but only offline.
pattiforniture.ch1_p2: Working in synergy with the Carnova agency, the challenge was to transform a complex corporate offer into a clear, authoritative, and accessible browsing experience.
pattiforniture.ch2_title1: "Transfer the solidity and assortment of the physical store into a digital infrastructure oriented towards clarity and conversion."
pattiforniture.ch3_p1: Working with a pre-existing visual identity — the logo was the only available asset — I focused entirely on two things: information architecture and tone of voice. An industrial B2B supplies company faces a specific communication challenge: its value is enormous, but difficult to make visually engaging online. I chose not to try to make it glamorous — I chose to make it clear, authoritative, and reassuring. Like a high-quality corporate brochure, but digital and navigable.
pattiforniture.ch3_p2: I designed a layout capable of giving breathing room to the company's various macro-sectors, organizing services, equipment, and brands in logical sections. The copywriting was designed to adopt a professional, reassuring, and service-oriented tone of voice, speaking effectively to both the B2B target and the consumer.
pattiforniture.ch4_p1: The infrastructure was developed entirely on the WordPress platform, optimizing content management to allow the company to display its offer in a structured way.
pattiforniture.ch4_p2: In addition to taking care of the layout of each individual view and perfect mobile responsiveness, I focused attention on conversion paths: quick calls, WhatsApp buttons, and quote request forms are strategically positioned to transform traffic into real commercial contacts.
pattiforniture.ch5_p1: The result is a web platform that precisely reflects the company's solidity — and finally makes it visible where its clients are looking. A project that shows how complex, in its own way, the challenge of communicating an industrial B2B business online truly is: it's not about adding aesthetics to something functional, but about finding the right visual language to convey value to someone who doesn't know you yet. The client received the result with great satisfaction.

sicilcosmetic.meta_desc: An end-to-end PrestaShop e-commerce for SicilCosmetic. Catalog management, UI/UX design, copywriting, and complete sales configuration.
sicilcosmetic.hero_desc: An end-to-end e-commerce project built on the PrestaShop platform for the Carnova agency. Integral care of the digital ecosystem: from user interface design to content drafting, up to technical configuration and management of the entire catalog.
sicilcosmetic.ch1_p1: SicilCosmetic serves both beauty industry professionals (barbers and hairdressers) and the consumer market, with a vast and fragmented catalogue: hair products, professional equipment, cosmetics, accessories — very different brands with inconsistent photo quality. The main challenge wasn't technical: it was organisational. How to transform a complex inventory, with non-uniform imagery and overlapping categories, into a smooth shopping experience that inspires trust at first glance?
sicilcosmetic.ch2_title1: "Organize beauty: transform a complex catalog into a fluid, intuitive and conversion-oriented shopping experience."
sicilcosmetic.ch3_p1: I took full care of the graphic layout and information architecture, designing a navigation system divided by macro-target (Men, Women) and specific need (Styling, Hair Care, Beard, Equipment). The decision to categorise by target on the homepage — rather than by brand or product type — was a deliberate UX choice: someone arriving on a beauty e-commerce already knows whether they're a professional or a consumer, but often doesn't yet know which brand they're looking for. Starting from the user's identity rather than the supplier catalogue reduces search time and increases conversion probability.
sicilcosmetic.ch3_p2: On a content level, I organized and laid out the information so that it responded to both SEO positioning logic and the need for clarity of the final buyer.
sicilcosmetic.ch4_p1: The sales infrastructure relies entirely on PrestaShop. In addition to the visual aspect, I personally took care of all the technical configuration "under the hood": from setting up payment methods and shipping rules, up to optimizing the checkout process.
sicilcosmetic.ch4_p2: Every page was structured to guarantee loading speed and perfect mobile responsiveness — critical for an e-commerce where most purchases happen on smartphones. Payment method configuration and shipping rules were optimised to reduce cart abandonment in the final stage, statistically the highest point of loss in any e-commerce.
sicilcosmetic.ch5_p1: The result is an online store that combines the elegance of the beauty world with the efficiency of a true sales machine. A project that demonstrates the ability to orchestrate in total autonomy the creation of a complex e-commerce, taking care with the same methodical precision of both the aesthetics of the visual front-end and the technical engine necessary to generate turnover.

newpop.meta_desc: The e-commerce of excellence in furniture and design. PrestaShop e-commerce project carried out in collaboration with the Carnova agency.
newpop.hero_desc: The e-commerce of excellence in furniture and design. Project carried out in collaboration with the Carnova agency, fully taking care of the graphic layout, the user interface (UI/UX), and part of the technical configuration of the PrestaShop infrastructure.
newpop.ch1_p1: Newpop is a showcase of excellence dedicated to interior design, lighting, and home decor — from Artemide to Smeg, from Fatboy to Le Creuset. Iconic products, brands with decades of history, pieces customers buy not because they need them but because they love them. The problem with a design e-commerce is that the product communicates by itself — if you let it. The challenge was to build an interface disciplined enough to disappear into the background, leaving all space for the pieces on display. An invisible interface that sells without appearing to.
newpop.ch2_title1: "Put yourself at the service of signature design: an invisible interface that leaves the stage to the beauty of the products, guiding the user towards a natural conversion."
newpop.ch3_p1: I took care of the entire graphic design starting from the assumption that the site design should never overpower the products. I organized the huge catalog into clean macro-thematic categories (Furniture, Table & Kitchen, Lighting, Outdoor), allowing fluid navigation.
newpop.ch3_p2: The strategic use of white space, combined with elegant typography and generous product image dimensions, created an 'art gallery' display where the bold colours of objects and their forms become the absolute protagonists. The main technical difficulty was migrating the catalogue to PrestaShop while maintaining the integrity of all data — images, variants, prices, SEO — a complex, high-error-risk operation requiring methodical attention.
newpop.ch4_p1: In support of visual design, I worked alongside the development team in the technical configuration based on PrestaShop. My intervention focused on optimizing the user experience at a structural level: from implementing search filters for designers, up to the care of the navigation mega-menu and the correct formatting of product carousels.
newpop.ch4_p2: The technical goal was to ensure that the loading speed and stability of the e-commerce were impeccable, even in the presence of thousands of references.
newpop.ch5_p1: The result is a digital boutique with international scope, where refined aesthetics meets modern e-commerce logic. A project that demonstrates something precise: in luxury design, the site must not 'sell' — it must 'exhibit'. The user doesn't purchase an object: they purchase an inspiration, a vision of what their home could look like. The role of design is to make that vision as vivid as possible.

bagliolauria.meta_desc: Website for an 18th-century agriturismo and charming events venue in the Sicilian countryside. UI/UX, copywriting and WordPress development with integrated booking system, built for Carnova.
bagliolauria.hero_desc: A complete digital project for a charming agriturismo nestled among olive groves and vineyards near the Valley of the Temples. Two souls to tell in one platform: rural hospitality for stays, and scenic elegance for weddings and exclusive events.
bagliolauria.ch1_title1: The charm of Made in Sicily.
bagliolauria.ch1_p1: Surrounded by olive groves and vineyards near the Valley of the Temples, Baglio Lauria is a charming property combining rural hospitality with the elegance of a wedding and events venue. The baglio — a former Franciscan hermitage acquired by the Lauria family in the 19th century — carries three centuries of history in its stone walls, arches, and pool overlooking the Agrigento countryside. The challenge was to translate all of this into a website that was, above all, emotional.
bagliolauria.ch2_title1: "Convey the warmth of the Sicilian sun and the elegance of ancient stone through an interface that makes the user dream from the very first click — whether they're looking for a night of relaxation or the perfect venue for the most important day of their life."
bagliolauria.ch3_p1: The complexity of this project lay in the dual audience: guests seeking a relaxing stay, and couples (or wedding planners) looking for an events venue. I structured the information architecture to accommodate both harmoniously — two parallel paths that intersect without ever merging. The stays section emphasises peace and authenticity; the events section uses photography of the pool and outdoor spaces to help visitors picture their perfect day.
bagliolauria.ch3_p2: The photographic material was generous and high quality — one of the most valuable gifts in a hospitality project. I chose to showcase it with an open, breathing layout, paired with serif/sans-serif typography that echoed the balance between the baglio's history and the contemporary experience it offers. The copywriting alternates emotional narrative and practical information — the reader must feel the scent of olive groves, but must also understand in thirty seconds how to book a room or request a wedding quote.
bagliolauria.ch4_p1: The entire ecosystem was built on WordPress, with particular attention to mobile responsiveness — because someone searching for a special events venue often browses from their phone, in a moment of pause, showing the site to their partner. Every view was designed to be emotional even on a small screen. It was one of my first complex projects, which makes the result all the more meaningful: it shows that attention to detail and listening to context produce solid work regardless of accumulated experience.
bagliolauria.ch4_p2: A key integration was the external booking link system, which guides visitors from initial inspiration through to availability requests for their stay or event. Contact forms and calls to action are positioned organically and non-invasively, respecting the emotional rhythm of the browsing experience.
bagliolauria.ch5_p1: The result is a website that breathes the same quiet air as the Agrigento countryside surrounding it. It was one of my first complete projects — and that makes it personally significant. Not because it's imperfect, but because it proves that even while growing, attention to detail and listening to the client produce results worth being proud of. The integrated booking system simplified the enquiry process for both stays and events. The client was delighted, and the site is live at bagliolauria.com.

villamima.meta_desc: WordPress site for a premier Sicilian wedding and events venue. UI/UX focused on visual storytelling of chef's food design and architecture. Project built for Carnova.
villamima.hero_label: UI/UX DESIGN • WEB & CONTENT • WEDDING & EVENTS
villamima.hero_desc: A premier wedding and events venue nestled among olive groves near the Valley of the Temples. A project where the interface design had one single goal: make the user feel the beauty before they read a single word.
villamima.ch1_p1: Villa Mima is far more than a reception hall: it is a complete sensory experience. The architecture, the Sicilian landscape, the chef's rigorous food design — every element combines to create an atmosphere the website needed to convey before the first contact. Working with Carnova, the challenge was to build a platform that made couples and wedding planners dream from the very first scroll — where every chef's dish is treated as a design object to display, not merely describe.
villamima.ch1_p2: Compared to Baglio Lauria — another project built for Carnova — Villa Mima had a different positioning: more oriented towards exclusivity, with the chef's food design as the central narrative element. Two sites born at different stages of my professional growth, with completely different palettes and visual approaches.
villamima.ch2_title1: "Elegance hides in the details: an interface designed to let users savour the magic of an unforgettable event — before the first taste."
villamima.ch3_p1: I developed a visual architecture that foregrounds emotion. The layout gives generous space to the venue's photography and the chef's artistic culinary creations: grid and carousel alternate to create visual rhythm without losing coherence. The choice to give the same visual weight to a dish and a corner of the villa was not accidental — it communicated that the Villa Mima experience is holistic: food is part of the spatial aesthetic, not an ancillary service.
villamima.ch3_p2: The serif typography chosen harmonises with the location's colours and style: elegant, never cold, with a warmth that echoes Sicilian stone and light. This project taught me to give even more space to design — to trust the image as the primary emotional vehicle, letting text play a supporting role.
villamima.ch4_p1: The entire ecosystem was engineered on WordPress, ensuring smooth loading despite the high density of photographic content. Time from brief to launch was approximately one month. The user experience was designed to remove every barrier to contact: the form is present and accessible, but never intrusive.
villamima.ch4_p2: Contact forms and calls to action are positioned organically within the navigation flow, inviting couples and planners to get in touch in a simple, empathetic way. High photographic density is managed with lazy loading and asset optimisation to ensure a smooth experience even on slower connections.
villamima.ch5_p1: The result is a website that smells of orange blossom and warm stone — and achieves this through images and composition, not words. A project confirming how visual maturity, gained project by project, radically changes the quality of the work: Villa Mima and Baglio Lauria speak the same language of Sicilian hospitality, but with completely different accents, built at different stages of my professional growth. The client expressed full satisfaction.

vinigambino.meta_desc: The essence of the volcanic terroir of Etna translated into an immersive digital experience. Project created for Cantina Gambino in collaboration with the Carnova agency.
vinigambino.hero_desc: The essence of the volcanic terroir translated into an immersive digital experience. Project created in collaboration with the Carnova agency for a historic winery on the slopes of Etna, fully taking care of the graphic layout, the user interface (UI/UX), and the layout on the WordPress platform.
vinigambino.ch1_title1: A sip of Etna online.
vinigambino.ch1_p1: Located on the northern slopes of Etna with views over the Gulf of Taormina, Cantina Gambino combines a winemaking tradition rooted in volcanic terroir with hospitality that invites the journey. The brief from Carnova was twofold: build an e-commerce space for the winery's volcanic wines — its sole label — and simultaneously convey the physical experience of the place: vineyards at over 700 metres altitude, the scents of lava rock, tastings with the volcano as backdrop, to convert international visitors into real guests.
vinigambino.ch2_title1: "Translating the power of the volcano and the elegance of wine into a visual journey that invites tasting, even before uncorking the bottle."
vinigambino.ch3_p1: I took full creative direction of the graphic design, building an interface that allowed the beauty of the vineyards and volcanic rock to breathe. The colour palette was derived directly from the landscape: warm, earthy tones echoing solidified lava, autumnal vineyards, basalt stone — with accents evoking the ruby of the wine. Editorial typography, in a serif/sans-serif pairing, guides the user through what needed to feel like a narrative tour, not a product sheet.
vinigambino.ch3_p2: The UX architecture for the tasting booking flow was carefully structured: the journey from the winery's story to the discovery of food and wine packages through to the booking request needed to be fluid and natural — like following the Gambino family narrative without ever feeling the friction of a commercial transaction. The site speaks two languages and addresses an international audience seeking authentic wine experiences beyond conventional tourism circuits.
vinigambino.ch4_p1: All the design was declined and engineered on the WordPress platform. My work focused on building dynamic and high-performance layouts, capable of hosting high-resolution photographs without compromising loading speed.
vinigambino.ch4_p2: I carefully laid out every section — from the bottle shop to the estate presentation pages — guaranteeing an impeccable and responsive visual experience on every device, allowing the company to communicate its prestige on a global scale.
vinigambino.ch5_p1: The result is a website that captures the soul of a terroir unique in the world — and does so through design tools, not words. The client appreciated the creative direction enormously, recognising in the site a digital identity coherent with the winery's premium positioning. A project demonstrating that graphic design is not embellishment, but the primary instrument for translating the quality of a physical product into digital emotion — and emotion into conversion.

loghi.meta_desc: Gallery of brand marks and visual identity elements designed to tell stories of excellence with geometric precision and contemporary sensibility. Logo design for Mapi Creazioni, Villa Masami and Sicef.
loghi.hero_label: BRAND GUIDELINES • LOGO DESIGN • VISUAL IDENTITY
loghi.hero_desc: Not mere graphic signs, but visual systems that tell stories before a single word is read. Every logo begins with a precise process: listening to the client, analysing the sector, searching for a visual idea that is scalable, lasting, and impossible to confuse with any other brand.

villamasami.role: Brand & Logo Design • UI/UX Design • Web
villamasami.description: The Villa Masami identity was born from a geometric intuition: merging the M and V of the name into a single, clean, scalable pictogram. Approved on the second proposal, the mark functions as logo, favicon, stamp, and decoration — a visual system built to last and adapt to any surface. The warm palette and balanced typography complete an identity that conveys the quiet elegance of Sicilian hospitality without stereotypes.

sicef.description: Sicef is a corporate brand requiring immediate authority and scalable recognisability. The choice of Lato — strong, geometric, international — conveys institutional solidity. The 's' with its diagonal cut becomes an autonomous pictogram: an icon that lives independently of the logotype and functions at any scale and in any context, from email signature to corporate signage.

mapicreazioni.description: Mapi Creazioni crafts objects entirely by hand. The logo tells this story with an essential pictogram: needle and thread, drawn with a thin, elegant stroke that mirrors the precision of handmade work. The Sacramento font adds the calligraphic touch of the artisan's signature — personal, authentic, impossible to replicate. A logo worth as much as what it represents.

portfolio.title: Ilaria Diliberto Portfolio
portfolio.description: A portfolio that changes its skin depending on who's looking. A dual-identity digital system, built to prove that a portfolio can itself be the most complex project in the portfolio.
portfolio.ch1_p1: The brief was personal: build something that didn't just showcase the work, but embodied the method. The solution was a live-switchable dual design system — Editorial and Nebula.
portfolio.ch2_p1: Challenge yourself technically, without losing warmth. Every technical decision needed a design rationale.
portfolio.fase1_desc: Two coherent and distinct visual identities — Editorial and Nebula — live-switchable without reloading the page.
portfolio.fase2_desc: Every visual value abstracted into CSS variables swapped at root level for total systemic consistency.
portfolio.fase3_desc: Framer Motion, Three.js, Web Audio API and a favicon that dynamically changes on theme toggle.
